subject: Connectivity selection for private inference pilot — gateway modes & tradeoffs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@edgebridge.com>, EdgeBridge NetOps <netops@edgebridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Private inference pilot — initial connectivity options and asks

Hi Claire / EdgeBridge team,

Thanks again for agreeing to the private inference pilot next quarter. We sketched three pragmatic connectivity approaches for the pilot:

1) Direct VPC peering (cloud-to-cloud) — simple L3 routing, lowest network hop count, but requires cross-account routing changes and can be noisy if you want fine-grained tenant isolation.

2) Interface endpoint / PrivateLink-style model (endpoint service) — stable, private L4/L7 connection with finer access controls and simpler whitelisting; avoids peering mesh but adds an endpoint management surface.

3) Site-to-site IPSec tunnel (S2S VPN) — quickest to stand up for on-prem, no cloud account changes required; higher latency variability and less friendly for large-scale multi-region setups.

I've attached a short connectivity matrix and a high-level diagram that summarize bandwidth, typical latency ranges, operational blast radius, and required NetOps actions. For the pilot we think Option 2 (interface endpoint) is a pragmatic default if you want per-service access controls; Option 3 is the fastest for your on-prem lab.

Can you confirm:
- Which of these aligns best with your compliance/segmentation needs?
- Do you have a preferred approach for private key exchange (KMS/HSM) and route acceptance windows?
- Are there Firewalls/NAT devices on your side that will require special NAT traversal or keepalives?

Proposed next steps: schedule a 30m networking sync the week of 12/14 to finalize the pilot mode and timeline.

Attachments: connectivity-matrix-v1.xlsx (summary table), inference-pilot-highlevel-diagram.png

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: EdgeBridge NetOps <netops@edgebridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Park <cpark@edgebridge.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private inference pilot — initial connectivity options and asks

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary and the matrix. Quick replies inline: 

- Compliance/segmentation: we need flow-level isolation between test tenants and production services. PrivateLink gives us per-service ACLs which is appealing.
- Key exchange: we prefer Certificate-based mutual auth for tunnels; for cloud endpoints we'll rely on mutual TLS backed by our internal PKI.
- Firewalls: our on-prem lab sits behind a stateful NAT and an enterprise firewall (F5). We'll need to open outbound UDP 4500/500 for IPSec if we go that route.

Question: if we choose PrivateLink, can Redwood provide a per-tenant endpoint name so our DNS team can create split-horizon records? Also, what's the expected egress IP footprint for the endpoint so we can lock down ACLs?

We can do a technical sync next Tuesday (12/15) AM.

— EdgeBridge NetOps
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: EdgeBridge NetOps <netops@edgebridge.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private inference pilot — initial connectivity options and asks

Claire / NetOps — great questions. Short answers and constraints from Redwood: 

- Per-tenant endpoints: yes — for PrivateLink we can create unique service endpoints scoped to your pilot tenants. We'll expose a stable DNS alias per tenant (tenantX-pilot.redwood.endpoint). We'll provide the DNS names and recommended CNAME records for split-horizon.

- Egress footprint: the endpoint will be served from our regional pool; for the pilot the egress CIDR range will be a small set of /24s (we will provide exact prefixes before cutover). Note that if you use VPC peering, source IPs remain your own; with PrivateLink the egress is owned by our service nodes.

- Operational tradeoffs:
  * Peering: low latency, simpler for large intra-cloud traffic, but requires cross-account IAM/route acceptance and complicates multi-region expansion.
  * PrivateLink: good for least-privilege access and simpler NetOps ops on your side; slightly higher application-layer complexity (endpoint management, DNS).
  * S2S VPN: fastest to prove in the lab; we suggest it for PoC only because it doesn't scale as cleanly.

We'll bring the endpoint naming plan and the egress CIDRs to the sync on 12/15. Agenda: 1) confirm pilot model; 2) exchange cert/KMS plan (if VPN), 3) validate firewall/NAT rules, 4) agree on go/no-go criteria.

Kimberly
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Claire Park <cpark@edgebridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeBridge NetOps <netops@edgebridge.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private inference pilot — initial connectivity options and asks

Thanks — that clarifies a lot. We'll aim for PrivateLink for the pilot to satisfy isolation and Prod/Test separation, but will stand up a temporary IPSec tunnel in parallel so our SREs can stress the path and collect latency stats.

Action items on our side before 12/15:
- DNS team will create the split-horizon zone (expected to be done 12/14 EOD).
- NetOps will validate that outbound 443 is allowed to Redwood's endpoint IPs; we'll verify once you send the CIDR list.
- SREs will provision a small VM for VPN testing and share AWS account number for the peering/endpoint attachment.

Looking forward to the sync — please include the matrix and the diagram in the calendar invite.

Claire
Head of Cloud Platform, EdgeBridge
